definition: The study of understanding how and why an AI model produces its outputs, often by examining its internal representations and computations.
details: Interpretability research (including mechanistic interpretability) aims to open the 'black box' of neural networks, which is important both for debugging model behavior and for building justified trust in high-stakes deployments.
story: Imagine a new medicine that works brilliantly in the lab but still has to be tested on real people before anyone takes it. In plain words: The study of understanding how and why an AI model produces its outputs, often by examining its internal representations and computations. Here is how it actually plays out: Interpretability research (including mechanistic interpretability) aims to open the 'black box' of neural networks, which is important both for debugging model behavior and for building justified trust in high-stakes deployments. Rules and red-teaming are the brakes that make the speed trustworthy. That deliberate caution is Interpretability.
